Rashi on Gittin 20b:10:1.english: And behold, he - [This refers to] the slave:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:10:2.hebrew: יוצא מתחת ידה - שהביאתו לפנינו ואמרה: "בעלי נתן לי העבד הזה וגירשני בו", כדתנן במתני': "ונותן לה העבד":
Rashi on Gittin 20b:10:2.english: Emerges from her possession - That she brought him before us and said, "My husband gave me this slave and divorced me with him," as we learned in the Mishnah: "And he gives her the slave."

Rashi on Gittin 20b:10:3.hebrew: מהו - מי מהימנה בלא עדי מסירה, הואיל ועכשיו הוא ברשותה, או דילמא הוא מנפשיה אזל:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:10:3.english: What is [the halakha] - Is she believed without witnesses of delivery, since he is now in her possession, or perhaps he went [to her] on his own:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:12:1.hebrew: להזדייף הוא - דילמא תנאה הוה בגיטא, ומחקתיה והדר כתביה:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:12:1.english: [It is writing that can] be forged - Perhaps there was a condition in the get [bill of divorce], and she erased it and then rewrote it:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:13:1.english: With witnesses of transmission - who read it:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:13:2.hebrew: ור' אלעזר היא - דאמר אי אפשר לגט בלא עדי מסירה:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:13:2.english: And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar - who says [that] a get cannot [be valid] without witnesses of delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:13:3.english: However, for Rami bar Chama it is difficult - for his question is [about a case] where there are no witnesses to the delivery:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:14:1.english: Tattooed writing - It is never erased:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:15:1.hebrew: הגודרות - בהמות, על שם "גדרות צאן" (במדבר לב):
Rashi on Gittin 20b:15:1.english: Hagodrot - [This means] livestock, named after [the phrase] "sheepfolds [gidrot tzon]" (Numbers 32):

Rashi on Gittin 20b:15:2.hebrew: אין להן חזקה - אדם שתפסן אינו יכול לטעון לבעליהם "מכרתם לי", דאיכא למימר מעצמן הלכו אצלו:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:15:2.english: There is no presumption [of ownership] for them - A person who took hold of them cannot claim to their owners, "You sold [them] to me," because it can be said [that] they went to him on their own:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:16:1.english: And behold, it emerges from his possession - [meaning] that he is coming to divorce her [with it]:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:16:2.hebrew: לא ידעה לאקנויי - לא גמרה ומקנייה דבר שאין בלבה לתת מתנה גמורה, ולא גירשה אלא בשלה, ואנן בעינן "ונתן":
Rashi on Gittin 20b:16:2.english: Does not know [how] to transfer ownership - She does not resolve to transfer ownership of something that she does not intend to give as an absolute gift, and [thus] he has only divorced her with her own [property], whereas we require [the verse's condition], "and he shall give [it]" [from his own].

Rashi on Gittin 20b:17:1.hebrew: אף הוא העיד - רבי יהודה בן בבא, במס' עדיות:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:17:1.english: Even he testified - [This refers to] Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, in Tractate Eduyot:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:17:2.hebrew: ה"ג: והא בעינא "ספר מקנה" וליכא - שהמקנה צריך לכתוב את השטר "שדי מכורה לך", דמההוא קרא נפקא לן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כו.):
Rashi on Gittin 20b:17:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: "And isn't there a need [for] 'a deed of purchase,' and it is not [fulfilled]?" - [Meaning] that the one transferring ownership must write the document [stating], "My field is sold to you," for we derive [this] from that verse in the first chapter of Kiddushin (26a):

Rashi on Gittin 20b:18:1.hebrew: אלא לאו - ש"מ כי מקני ליה, שפיר דמי, ואף על גב דאין בדעתו של נותן שיעכבנו המקבל אצלו:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:18:1.english: Rather, is it not - Learn from this [that] when he transfers [ownership of] it to him, it is valid, even though it is not the giver's intention that the recipient keep it in his possession:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:1:1.english: Isn't there a need [for] "writing" - [That is, "writing,] the engravings of a signet" [Exodus 39:30]:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:1:2.hebrew: מגואי - מכה הרושם באותו צד שהצורה בולטת בו, אבל ציץ דוחק מאבראי והיא בולטת מגואי:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:1:2.english: From the inside - He strikes the stamp on the same side on which the form protrudes, whereas [with the] tzitz [frontplate], he presses from the outside and it protrudes on the inside:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:4:1.hebrew: הא ליכא שאר לא - דמקום גט בעי למיתב לה מתנה גמורה משום גירושין, ולא לשם פרעון, דכתיב "ונתן":
Rashi on Gittin 20b:4:1.english: [If] there is no remainder, no - because he must give her the space of the bill of divorce [as] an absolute gift for the sake of divorce, and not for the sake of payment, as it is written: "and he shall give":

Rashi on Gittin 20b:5:1.english: If he said to her - "[This is] for your marriage contract":

Rashi on Gittin 20b:7:1.english: And the paper [is mine] - [Meaning:] I am retaining the entire paper for myself:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:7:2.hebrew: אינה מגורשת - דכיון דהנייר שלו, לא נתן לה כלום, דנמצאו אותיות פורחות באויר:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:7:2.english: She is not divorced - For since the paper is his, he has not given her anything, as the letters turn out to be flying in the air:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:7:3.hebrew: הרי זו מגורשת - ותחזיר, דמתנה ע"מ להחזיר שמה מתנה:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:7:3.english: She is divorced - and she must return [the paper], because a gift [given] on condition to return [it] is called a gift:

Rashi on Gittin 20b:8:1.hebrew: נייר שבין שיטה לשיטה - שלי, מהו:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:8:1.english: The paper between [one] line and [another] line - [if he said, "it is] mine," what is [the law]?

Rashi on Gittin 20b:9:1.hebrew: דמעורה - מעורה במקצת, שהיו בו אותיות ארוכין המגיעין משיטה לשיטה בראשי כל תיבה ותיבה:
Rashi on Gittin 20b:9:1.english: Where [it is] intertwined - [It is] partially intertwined, in that there were long letters in it reaching from line to line at the beginnings of every word:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:14:1.hebrew: בכתובת קעקע - מדאורייתא ליכא איסורא עד שיכתוב ויקעקע בדיו ובכחול, כדתנן בפ"ג דמכות (דף כא.). ולר' שמעון אינו חייב אפי' כתב וקעקע, עד שיכתוב את השם — פי' שם דע"ז, כדמפרש התם בגמרא. ומיהו איסורא דרבנן איכא הכא, דאפי' אפר מקלה אסור ליתן על גבי מכתו, מפני שנראה ככתובת קעקע. ואפי' הויא הכא איסורא דאורייתא, מ"מ הוי גט, כדאמרי' לעיל: כתבו על איסורי הנאה כשר, אע"ג דאסור לכתוב, דהא מיתהני באיסורי הנאה:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:14:1.english: With a tattoo - By Torah law there is no prohibition unless one writes and tattoos with ink and with kohl, as we learned in the Mishnah in the third chapter of Makkot (21a). And according to Rabbi Shimon, one is not liable even if he wrote and tattooed unless he writes "the Name" — meaning, the name of an idol, as the Gemara explains there. However, there is a rabbinic prohibition here, for even wood-ash is forbidden to be placed upon one's wound, because it looks like a tattoo. And even if there were a Torah prohibition here, nevertheless it is a [valid] bill of divorce, as we said above: if he wrote it on items from which benefit is forbidden, it is valid, even though it is forbidden to write [on them], since he is thereby deriving benefit from items from which benefit is forbidden:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:15:1.hebrew: ת"ש דאמר ריש לקיש הגודרות אין להם חזקה - פי': לאלתר, אלא עד ג' שנים יש להם חזקה, כדאמרינן בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לו.). וא"ת, מתני' הוה ליה לאתויי, דתנן התם (דף כח.): "העבדים חזקתן ג' שנים מיום ליום", אבל לאלתר לא! ועוד, מאי קמ"ל ריש לקיש? מתני' היא! ודוחק לומר כמו שפי' הרב ר' יהודה מקורבי"ל, דריש לקיש אתא לאשמועינן אפי' בכה"ג דאיירי הכא שהגט כתוב על ידו או על קרן של פרה, דאיכא הוכחה קצת דיהביה לאשה, אפ"ה אין לה חזקה, ולהכי מייתי מר"ל; דא"כ הוה ליה לפרושי בהדיא, כיון דלא איצטריך לאשמועינן אלא בכי האי גוונא! אלא י"ל דממתני' לא שמעינן גודרות, דה"א דוקא עבדים דבני דעת ועיילי מנפשייהו, אבל גודרות אין דרכם לילך לבית איש נכרי, ולהכי ה"א הכא שהגט כתוב על ידו ומוכח קצת שהוא שלה יש לה חזקה; להכי מייתי מגודרות, דאין להם חזקה אע"פ שיש הוכחה דלא עיילי מנפשייהו כמו עבדים:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:15:1.english: Come and hear, as Reish Lakish said: Livestock have no presumption [of ownership] - Meaning: immediately [upon taking possession]; rather, [only] after three years do they have a presumption [of ownership], as we say in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 36a). And if you ask: [the Gemara] should have cited the Mishnah, as we learned there (28a): "Slaves, their presumption [of ownership] is three years from day to day," [which implies] that immediately [they do] not [have a presumption of ownership]! And furthermore, what is Reish Lakish teaching us? It is [already] a Mishnah! And it is forced to say as Rabbi Yehudah of Corbeil explained, that Reish Lakish comes to teach us [that] even in a case such as this, which we are discussing here, where the bill of divorce is written on his hand or on the horn of a cow, where there is somewhat of a proof that he gave it to the woman, even so, she has no presumption [of ownership], and therefore [the Gemara] cites from Reish Lakish; for if so, [Reish Lakish] should have explained [this] explicitly, since [his statement] was only needed to teach us [the law] in such a case! Rather, one can say that from the Mishnah we would not derive [the law for] livestock, for one might have thought [that] specifically slaves, who have intelligence and enter [a house] on their own, [have no immediate presumption of ownership], whereas livestock do not typically go into the house of a stranger, and therefore one might have thought [that] here, where the bill of divorce is written on his hand and it is somewhat evident that he belongs to her, she has a presumption [of ownership]; therefore, [the Gemara] cites from [the case of] livestock, that they have no presumption [of ownership] even though there is proof [in that] they do not enter on their own like slaves:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:16:1.hebrew: אשה לא ידעה לאקנויי - פירוש: בדבר שהוא מחזיר לה, ולא גמרה ומיקניא ליה, אלא בתורת שאילה משאילתו לו. אע"ג דאמרי' לעיל דדמי כתיבת סופר אקנו ליה רבנן מדידה, מ"מ טבלא דידה לא מקנו ליה. וא"ת: וכי לא ידע מתני' [דכותבת] דפשיט מינה בסמוך דהאשה כותבת את גיטה? וי"ל: דמצי לדחויי דכותבת על קלף דבעל, אלא שנותנת שכר הכתיבה. ורב אשי דפשיט מינה, משמע ליה דאיירי בקלף שלה:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:16:1.english: A woman does not know how to transfer ownership - Meaning: regarding something that he returns to her, and she does not sincerely resolve to transfer ownership [of it] to him, but rather lends it to him as a loan. Even though we said above that the Rabbis transferred to him the cost of the scribe's writing from her [property], nevertheless they did not transfer her slate to him. And if you will say: Did [Rami bar Ḥama] not know the Mishnah [of "she writes"], from which [Rav Ashi] resolves [the dilemma] immediately below, that a woman writes her [own] bill of divorce? One can say: [Rami bar Ḥama] could deflect [this proof by saying] that she writes [it] on the husband's parchment, except that she pays the fee for the writing. Whereas Rav Ashi, who resolves [the dilemma] from it, understands that it is speaking of her [own] parchment:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:17:1.hebrew: וכותב בכתב ידו ואחרים חותמים - ואם תאמר, מה ענין שטרי הלואה לגט? דאינם אלא לראיה, ואפי' במלוה על פה היה גובה ממשעבדי, אי לא משום דאין לה קול, כדאמרינן בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב מב.) דמאן דיזיף בצנעה יזיף, ומכר שיש לו קול אמרינן (שם מא:): "המוכר שדהו בעדים גובה מנכסים משועבדים". ונראה לפרש, דנראה לגמרא דמסתמא כיון שהיה מלוה לכל בני העיר, גם הם היו עושים לו טובה, ונותנים לו במתנה או מוכרים לו שדות, דפעמים שלא היו קנויין לו אלא בשטר, כגון "שדי נתונה לך" או "מכורה לך", וגם השטרות האלו היה כותב אותם ואחרים חותמים:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:17:1.english: And he would write in his handwriting and others would sign - And if you will say: What is the relevance of loan documents to a bill of divorce? For they are only for proof, and even with an oral loan one would collect from encumbered property, were it not for [the fact] that it has no publicity, as we say in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 42a), that whoever borrows, borrows in private; whereas [regarding] a sale, which has publicity, we say (there, 41b): "One who sells his field before witnesses collects from encumbered property." And it seems [right] to explain that it appears to the Gemara that presumably, since he would lend to all the residents of the town, they too would do him favors and give him [fields] as a gift or sell him fields, where sometimes they were not acquired by him except through a document — such as [writing], "My field is given to you" or "sold to you" — and these documents too he would write and others would sign:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:2:1.hebrew: התקבלי גיטיך והתקבלי כתובתיך מהו - אע"ג דכתבו על איסורי הנאה כשר, היינו משום דיהיב לה מיהא כל הגט; אבל הכא לא יהיב לה אלא בתורת פרעון:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:2:1.english: Receive your bill of divorce and receive your marriage contract, what is [the halakha] - Even though if he wrote it on [items from which] benefit is forbidden it is valid, that is because he nevertheless gives her the entire bill of divorce; whereas here, he only gives it to her as payment:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:7:1.hebrew: על מנת שתחזירי לי הנייר מגורשת - בפרק מי שאחזו (לקמן גיטין דף עה.) קבעי מ"ש רישא ומ"ש סיפא, ומפרש לשון אחד: משום דסיפא הוי תנאי ומעשה בדבר אחד, והוי תנאי בטל ומעשה קיים; דקסבר ההוא לישנא דאומר ע"מ לאו כאומר מעכשיו דמי, ואין גט יכול לחול עד שתחזירהו, ואז א"א להתגרש שאין הגט בידה, הילכך אע"פ שלא החזירתו מגורשת. ורבא דקאמר בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ו:) "הילך אתרוג זה במתנה ע"מ שתחזירו לי, החזירו יצא כו'", לא סבר כההוא לישנא, אלא רבא לטעמיה, דמפרש בפ' מי שאחזו משום דהוי מעשה קודם לתנאי. ואע"ג דבההיא דאתרוג נמי מעשה קודם לתנאי, לא דק רבא במילתיה למינקט התנאי כמו שצריך להתנות. ולההוא לישנא דמפרש במי שאחזו (לקמן גיטין עד.) משום דכל האומר ע"מ כאומר מעכשיו דמי, לא הוי גט אלא אם כן החזירתו לבסוף שנתקיים התנאי, ואז הוי גט משעה שבא לידה:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:7:1.english: On the condition that you return the paper to me, she is divorced - In the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (below, Gittin 75a), [the Gemara] asks: What is different [in] the first clause, and what is different [in] the second clause? And one version explains: because [in] the second clause, it is a condition and an act in one [and the same] thing, and [therefore] the condition is void and the act stands; for that version holds that one who says "on condition that" is not like one who says "from now," and [thus] a get cannot take effect until she returns it, and then it is impossible to be divorced because the get is not in her hand; therefore, even though she did not return it, she is divorced. And Rava, who says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (6b): "Here is this etrog for you as a gift on condition that you return it to me; [if] he returned it, he has fulfilled [his obligation], etc." — does not hold like that version, but rather Rava [follows] his own reasoning, as he explains in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo, [that the difference between the clauses is] because it is an act [that] precedes the condition. And even though in that [case] of the etrog as well, the act precedes the condition, Rava was not exact in his phrasing to state the condition as it needs to be stipulated. And according to that [other] version that explains in Mi She'achazo (below, Gittin 74a) [that it is] because anyone who says "on condition that" is like one who says "from now," it is not a [valid] get unless she returns it at the end, when the condition is fulfilled, and then it is a [valid] get from the time it came into her hand:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:9:1.hebrew: ספר אחד אמר רחמנא ולא שנים ושלשה ספרים - אע"ג דלקמן (גיטין דף כא:) דרשי רבנן "ספר" לספירת דברים, מכל מקום דרשי' נמי הך דרשה דהכא. וא"ת: היכי מכשירין בפ' בתרא (לקמן גיטין דף פז:): "שייר מקצת הגט וכתבו בדף השני"? הוה לן למיפסל בשני דפין משום "ספר אחד אמר רחמנא ולא שנים ושלשה ספרים", כדאמרי' בפ"ב דסוטה (דף יח.): כתבה בשני דפין פסולה, ספר אחד אמר רחמנא כו'! ואור"י דשני דפים דסוטה איירי בשתי חתיכות, ולקמן איירי בקלף אחד בשני עמודים:
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:9:1.english: The Merciful One said one scroll, and not two or three scrolls - Even though later (Gittin 21b) the Rabbis expound "scroll" (sefer) [as teaching] the recounting of words, nevertheless, we also expound this exposition here. And if you ask: How do we validate in the last chapter (later, Gittin 87b) [a case where] one left over part of the get and wrote it in the second column? We should invalidate [it] on two columns because "the Merciful One said one scroll, and not two or three scrolls," as we say in the second chapter of Sotah (18a): [If] one wrote it on two columns, it is invalid — "the Merciful One said one scroll," etc.! And R"I says that the two columns of Sotah refers to two [separate] pieces [of parchment], whereas later [in Gittin] it refers to one parchment with two columns:

Tosafot on Gittin 20b:9:2.hebrew: לא צריכא דמעורה - מכאן מדקדק ר' יצחק בר מרדכי, דאין צריך בגט שתהא כל אות ואות מוקפת גויל מארבע רוחותיה, כדאמר הכא "דמעורה". ור"י אומר דאין מכאן ראיה, דהא דקאמר "דמעורה", היינו רגל ך' של שיטה עליונה בט' של שיטה שתחתיה, או ראש ל' בה' או בח' שלמעלה הימנה. ומ"מ נראה לר"י דאין צריך ראיה להכשיר, דדוקא בס"ת, תפילין ומזוזות בעינן שיהו האותיות מוקפות גויל, כדאמר בפרק הקומץ (מנחות דף לד.), משום דכתיב בהו "וכתבתם" — כתיבה תמה; אבל בגט ליכא קפידא, דאפי' ספר ודיו לא בעינן בגט, ד"ספר" דכתב בגט, לספירת דברים הוא דאתא (לקמן גיטין כא:):
Tosafot on Gittin 20b:9:2.english: No, it is necessary [where it is] intertwined - From here Rabbi Yitzchak bar Mordekhai infers that a bill of divorce does not require each and every letter to be surrounded by blank parchment on all four sides, since [the Gemara] says here, "where it is intertwined." However, Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that there is no proof from here, for what [the Gemara] means by "intertwined" is [for example] the leg of a final kaf of an upper line [extending] into a tet of the line below it, or the top of a lamed into a heh or a chet above it. Nevertheless, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that no proof is needed to validate [such a bill of divorce], for it is specifically in a Torah scroll, tefillin, and mezuzot that we require the letters to be surrounded by blank parchment, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] HaKometz (Menachot 34a), because it is written regarding them, "and you shall write them" — [meaning] perfect writing; but regarding a bill of divorce there is no such requirement, for we do not even require a scroll or ink for a bill of divorce, since [the word] "sefer" that is written regarding a bill of divorce comes [only] for the recounting of matters (below, Gittin 21b):
